import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 1.74 (Tarski monster topologizability)

by V. P. Platonov

Problem 1.74 asks to describe all "minimal topological groups" in Platonov's
sense: non-discrete Hausdorff topological groups all of whose proper closed
subgroups are discrete. A natural test case: does there exist a Tarski monster
group admitting a non-discrete Hausdorff group topology? A Tarski monster
would be a minimal group in this sense, since all its proper subgroups are
finite (hence discrete in any Hausdorff group topology).

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v40)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«1.74»

/--
A Tarski monster group: an infinite group in which every non-trivial proper
subgroup has order a fixed prime $p$.
-/
def IsTarskiMonster (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  Infinite G ∧ ∃ p : ℕ, p.Prime ∧
    ∀ H : Subgroup G, H ≠ ⊥ → H ≠ ⊤ → Nat.card H = p

/--
Does there exist a Tarski monster group that admits a non-discrete Hausdorff
group topology?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20 22]
theorem kourovka_1_74 : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G) (_ : TopologicalSpace G),
      IsTarskiMonster G ∧ IsTopologicalGroup G ∧ T2Space G ∧
      ¬ DiscreteTopology G := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«1.74»

findings.description: The sole problem theorem (lines 49–52) asks only whether some Tarski monster admits a non-discrete Hausdorff group topology. Problem 1.74 instead asks for a classification of all Platonov-minimal topological groups. The module's proposed “natural test case” is not a question posed by the cited source, and answering it does not provide that classification. The restriction is genuinely narrower: the usual additive real group has every proper closed subgroup discrete, but is not a Tarski monster, since it contains the proper infinite subgroup ℤ. Both properties of the real-group example were verified in Lean.
findings.source_evidence: The Kourovka Notebook, https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v40, Problem 1.74 (LaTeX source 21tkt.tex, lines 432–436): “Describe all minimal topological groups, that is, non-discrete groups all of whose closed subgroups are discrete.” It adds that the locally compact case is easy but the general case is probably complicated. There is no Tarski-monster existence question. The same text appears in the current version at https://arxiv.org/html/1401.0300v46#p66.1.
findings.suggested_fix: Define Platonov minimality using non-discreteness and `∀ H : Subgroup G, H ≠ ⊤ → IsClosed (H : Set G) → DiscreteTopology H`, for Hausdorff topological groups, and formulate the requested complete characterization/classification of that class with an appropriate answer placeholder. The existing Tarski-monster existence statement could be retained as a separately sourced solved special case, but it should not replace Problem 1.74.

status_issues.source_status: The existence question actually formalized was answered affirmatively by Klyachko, Olshanskii, and Osin (2013), Theorem 1.4. They construct topologizable Tarski monsters of every sufficiently large odd exponent n. Taking n to be a sufficiently large odd prime p makes every nontrivial proper subgroup cyclic of order p, exactly as required by IsTarskiMonster. This does not settle Platonov's full classification problem.
status_issues.evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/1210.7895, version 3; Theorem 1.4 in https://arxiv.org/e-print/1210.7895v3 states: “For every sufficiently large odd n ∈ ℕ there exists a topologizable Tarski Monster of exponent n.” The paper defines topologizable as admitting a non-discrete Hausdorff group topology, and its monsters have all proper subgroups finite cyclic.
status_issues.suggested_change: If this existence statement is retained, mark it `research solved`, replace the placeholder by `answer(True)`, and cite Klyachko–Olshanskii–Osin. Do not mark the original classification problem solved on this basis.

reformulations.difference: The usual prime-order definition explicitly describes nontrivial proper subgroups as cyclic groups of order p. Lean requires only `Nat.card H = p`, without separate finiteness or cyclicity conditions.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Since p is prime, p ≠ 0. Consequently `Nat.card H = p` forces H to be finite; an infinite H would have Nat.card H = 0. Every group of prime order is cyclic. Conversely, a finite cyclic group of order p has Nat.card equal to p. A Lean equivalence with the formulation adding `Finite H ∧ IsCyclic H` for every nontrivial proper subgroup was proved in the scratch file.

sources_consulted: The Kourovka Notebook, arXiv:1401.0300v40: https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v40 and LaTeX source https://arxiv.org/e-print/1401.0300v40; Problem 1.74, its surrounding remarks, the preface's status conventions, and the distinct Tarski-monster convention in Problem 21.72.

A. A. Klyachko, A. Yu. Olshanskii, D. V. Osin, On topologizable and non-topologizable groups, Topology and its Applications 160 (2013), 2104–2120: https://arxiv.org/abs/1210.7895 and https://arxiv.org/e-print/1210.7895v3; definitions, Theorem 1.4, its context, and its proof.

Local Mathlib sources for Infinite, Nat.Prime, Nat.card and Cardinal.toNat, subgroup carriers and lattice extrema, prime-order cyclicity, IsTopologicalGroup, T2Space, DiscreteTopology, finite Hausdorff spaces, and discrete subgroups of Archimedean ordered groups; FormalConjecturesUtil/Answer.lean and Attributes/Basic.lean.
Local review guidance: STATEMENTS.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, AGENTS.md; calibration: /workspace/past_misformalizations/INDEX.md and pr04607.md, pr04103.md, pr04037.md, pr04595.md.

Added IsPlatonovMinimal with the Hausdorff, topological-group, non-discreteness, and proper-closed-subgroup conditions, and updated the documentation. IsTarskiMonster remains unchanged. The required compile command succeeds with only the expected sorry warning; scratch proofs verify the classification encoding and representative boundary cases.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Problem 1.74 (Minimal topological groups)

by V. P. Platonov

Problem 1.74 asks to describe all "minimal topological groups" in Platonov's
sense: non-discrete Hausdorff topological groups all of whose proper closed
subgroups are discrete. A Tarski monster admitting a non-discrete Hausdorff
group topology is minimal in this sense, since all its proper subgroups are
finite (hence discrete in any Hausdorff group topology).

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v40)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«1.74»

/--
A Tarski monster group: an infinite group in which every non-trivial proper
subgroup has order a fixed prime $p$.
-/
def IsTarskiMonster (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  Infinite G ∧ ∃ p : ℕ, p.Prime ∧
    ∀ H : Subgroup G, H ≠ ⊥ → H ≠ ⊤ → Nat.card H = p

/--
A minimal topological group in Platonov's sense: a non-discrete Hausdorff
topological group all of whose proper closed subgroups are discrete.
-/
def IsPlatonovMinimal (G : Type*) [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G] : Prop :=
  IsTopologicalGroup G ∧ T2Space G ∧ ¬ DiscreteTopology G ∧
    ∀ H : Subgroup G, H ≠ ⊤ → IsClosed (H : Set G) → DiscreteTopology H

/-- Describe all minimal topological groups in Platonov's sense. -/
@[category research open, AMS 20 22]
theorem kourovka_1_74 :
    {X : Σ G : Type, Group G × TopologicalSpace G |
      @IsPlatonovMinimal X.1 X.2.1 X.2.2} = answer(sorry) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«1.74»
